html:
SMTO-AUT-0005 — SMTO didn't run an admin command that was set up to take input

GUID: 058513d1-20a1-4d7a-9dfd-aaf655795459
Slug: privilege-capture-mode-required
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: aut

What happened

  • This command needs administrator rights, but it was set up to also take typed input or run interactively. SMTO keeps your administrator password apart from what the command reads, so it stopped before running anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reply in the conversation asking SMTO to run the command again without typing input into it, and to put that input in a file first. SMTO only sends your administrator password when the command reads no typed input, so the two can't get mixed up.
  2. If the command will take a long time, ask SMTO to run it as a background job. A background job is a supported way to run long administrator commands without typed input.

What success looks like

  • The command runs and its step is marked Elevated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the command you wanted to run, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't put your administrator password into the command or the Task request to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The sudo handler refused a privileged request before dispatch because it was not a captured, non-interactive shell_command with stdin_mode none, which managed elevation requires to keep sudo authentication input isolated.

What this means

  • Managed elevation requires captured noninteractive execution with authentication input isolated from command-owned stdin. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Managed elevation requires captured noninteractive execution with authentication input isolated from command-owned stdin.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare execution_mode, interaction_mode and stdin_mode with the managed privilege contract.

How to fix it

  • Re-issue the command as a shell_command with execution_mode='captured', interaction_mode='non_interactive' and stdin_mode='none' (prepare_shell in src/agent_runtime/execution/sudo_handler.py); pass task data through a command-owned heredoc or file, and use background=true when a durable job is needed. Do not resubmit the same request unchanged.
  • Use the supported privileged shell mode. Keep authentication input separate from command-owned stdin; use a heredoc or file for task data and background=true when a durable job is needed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The privileged request uses supported captured noninteractive mode and isolated authentication input.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
